beats.text: Couples who shared one bank account stayed happier. And that's an experiment!
Researchers took two hundred thirty engaged or newly married couples with separate accounts. And randomly told them: merge, stay separate, or do whatever you want.
Over two years, couples with separate accounts became less happy with their relationship. And the joint accounts?
No decline! And more in sync about money.
So love is shared. Maybe money too!

sources: Olson, Rick, Small & Finkel (2023), Common cents: Bank account structure and couples' relationship dynamics, Journal of Consumer Research 50(4) – 230 engaged/newlywed couples randomly assigned (joint / separate / no instruction), two years; joint-account couples avoided the decline in relationship quality and reported more financial harmony.
